| [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) v4 | Beyond the scalar linear Gaussian case and the deterministic case of a fast, contracting eliminated variable, when a coarse variable's reduced dynamics carry memory of the eliminated variables, does it admit a finite-dimensional Markovian augmentation whose prediction error is bounded in terms of the eliminated dynamics, and is a level whose history, not its present state, does the predicting still a level? | A3 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, A5's candidate Q3. The Mori–Zwanzig decomposition writes any projected dynamics as a Markovian term, a memory term and noise. The record holds no reading of it. Its criteria of closure ([THEORY-257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-257.md)) condition on the coarse variable's own history, so memory is not by itself a failure of them, and [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) already locates a collective in a variable members read from the past. | Open |
| [QUESTION-231](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-231.md) | Does Coifman and Lafon's α-normalized diffusion limit hold on a compact manifold with boundary, in L² on band-limited functions at a stated rate, and does the iterated operator P_{ε,α}^{t/ε} converge to the semigroup of the limit operator? | The boundary and semigroup halves of the promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md). [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md) was narrowed to compact manifolds without boundary and promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2), with the source's kernel expansion re-derived. What it does not settle: the limit near a boundary, at the rate the source prints, and the heat-kernel limit that the source's Proposition 11 claims. | Open |
| [QUESTION-240](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-240.md) | Does a transport whose local kernels commute with restriction preserve overlap consistency, and does a transport induced by one global stochastic kernel preserve global extendability? | The part of [QUESTION-022](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-022.md) the manuscript's Propositions 1 and 2 settle, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). Yes to both, for finite scenarios: [CLAIM-121](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-121.md) for overlap consistency and [CLAIM-070](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-070.md) for global extendability. Both are sufficient conditions. Whether they are necessary, and what transports that change the cover do, stays with [QUESTION-022](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-022.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-242](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-242.md) | Does exact dynamical closure of an aggregate require a nearly decomposable block, or can a collective variable be exactly dynamically independent when no partition of the units is weakly coupled? | The converse half of [QUESTION-221](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-221.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [CLAIM-388](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md): closure does not require a nearly decomposable block. In a linear Gaussian VAR(1) with uniform coupling, the sum of all units is exactly dynamically independent at every stable coupling strength, while every partition couples as strongly across its edges as within them. The forward bound stays with [QUESTION-221](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-221.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-245](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-245.md) | For linear decisions at the population level, if a kind's admissible transformations are given as a distribution over pairs of its realizations, is the top eigenspace of the pair operator a stable, decision-sufficient span, and what span takes that role when the pairs are directed? | The linear part of [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). For symmetric pairs, yes: the top eigenfunctions are the most view-invariant directions, and their span is minimax-optimal for linear prediction of approximately view-invariant targets ([THEORY-007](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-007.md)) and bounds linear-probe error by leakage over conductance ([THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md)). For directed pairs, the top left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator take that role ([THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md)), and a linear readout of the full density ratio suffices for redundant labels ([THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md)). Other spans can tie. Nonlinear decisions, and what picks one signature out, stay with [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-247](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-247.md) | If the communicative object is a presheaf of propositions over a category of contexts, is the negation its topos logic gives an orthocomplement or a Heyting pseudo-complement, and what fixes it? | The conditional part of [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) and [THEORY-037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md). Over a presheaf of contexts the truth values are sieves, and negation is the Heyting pseudo-complement that the base category fixes, not an orthocomplement. Whether the communicative object is such a presheaf, over which base, and whether probes split it into sectors, stays with [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-248](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-248.md) | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), does a scalar linear coarse variable whose reduced dynamics carry memory admit an exact finite-dimensional Markovian augmentation? | [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) for the linear Gaussian class, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [CLAIM-398](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-398.md). Yes: a scalar coarse variable Y = LX of a VAR(1) on ℝⁿ is an ARMA process of orders at most (n, n − 1). Its Mori–Zwanzig memory is non-zero at every lag in general, but finitely many coordinates, built from Y's own past and innovations, carry it exactly. Other classes, error in terms of the eliminated spectrum, and the ruling on levels stay with [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-251](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-251.md) | Do the Johnson–Lindenstrauss threshold for distances and the k log(N/k) threshold for sparse recovery rest on one concentration-of-measure argument, a tail bound for each fixed vector's norm with a union bound over a family, both for sufficiency and for necessity? | The part of [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md) its readings on distances and sparse recovery settle, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). For sufficiency, yes: one per-vector tail and a union bound give both, over pairs for distances ([THEORY-397](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-397.md)) and over net points on every sparse support for recovery ([THEORY-390](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-390.md)). For necessity, no: the distance lower bounds are encoding and bit-counting arguments ([THEORY-395](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-395.md), [THEORY-399](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-399.md)), recovery's rests on Gelfand widths, and its sharp location on face counting ([THEORY-391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md)). Random features, superposition and expand-and-threshold stay with [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-252](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-252.md) v3 | For the conditions an effective description is asked to meet (predictive sufficiency for a declared target, dynamical independence of the omitted variables, memory closure under a declared projection, approximation fidelity in a declared metric and horizon, and tractability within a declared budget), which can fail while all the others hold, which such configurations are impossible in which model classes, and which conditions turn out to be parameters of the others rather than conditions in their own right? | The owner's idea at U3 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "what if we censor or negate each virtue one at a time? that reduces our combinations from n! to n." A3 corrected the count (2ⁿ presence/absence configurations, not n!) and fixed five conditions, asking whether each leave-one-out case is realizable: "An impossible configuration is itself a substantive result." The record holds pairwise non-implications only, none a leave-one-out witness: [CLAIM-389](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md) gives zero memory without independence in VAR(1), [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) retention without feasible recovery. A4 and A5 then found that some conditions are parameters rather than conditions ([CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md)). The same form as [QUESTION-093](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-093.md) and [QUESTION-115](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md), on a new list. | Open |
| [QUESTION-255](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md) v5 | Can an empirical model that genuinely fails to glue, under a specified cover and correspondence between its contexts, take part in one phenomenally unified process, given that a unified experience can contain conflicting interpretations or demands and that such conflicts are not by themselves gluing obstructions? | A7 §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-21, after A6 found a sheaf-theoretic account of global phenomenal unity. The record's self line already reads a coherent self as a global section ([CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md)), and conflict without an overlap as no disunity ([CLAIM-198](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md)). A7 denied that experiential unity is "the existence of one globally consistent assignment of interpretations": "the conflict itself can be a unified experience", and a global assignment "could exist in a merely descriptive model without any corresponding unified process". A review of 2026-10-22 corrected the example: a felt conflict need not be a gluing failure, since one global state can hold both sides. The question is whether a model that genuinely fails to glue, under a cover and correspondence fixed independently, can be part of one unified experience. | Open |
| [QUESTION-272](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-272.md) v2 | When the task's target and the probes' outcome laws are both linear in one unknown state, as for the pairwise comparisons of actions under partial monitoring and for the authority shares of a mixture of known response profiles, when does a family of probes separate what the task needs told apart? | The part of [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) that the readings of 2026-10-25 settle, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). Both answers are linear: a probe family separates what the task needs exactly when the task's target lies in the span of what the probes reveal. For pairwise comparisons of actions under partial monitoring, that is the loss difference lying in the probes' combined signal row space ([THEORY-962](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-962.md)). For the authority shares of a mixture of known profiles, it is the profiles over the probe contexts being affinely independent ([CLAIM-452](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-452.md)). The general stochastic, decision-relative case, where the target or the outcome laws are not linear in a common state, stays with [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-282](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-282.md) | Under what conditions do interactions change the physically operative correspondence structure among systems (the compatibility operator itself, not only the states it relates), rather than merely reveal it to a measurement or redescribe it in a model? | Raised at the owner's review of the pull request that filed the exchange "Field Existence Question", which called it "one of the genuinely unfinished parts of the program". The formal results the record now holds take the correspondence structure as input. A sheaf's restriction maps, a gauge connection, a port condition and a Laplacian are given, and the mathematics says what follows. [CLAIM-471](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md)'s strong thesis is that interactions can make or change that structure. Only one model the record has read changes it through interaction, and there agreement is reached by learning to lie. The question asks for conditions under which the operative structure changes, with a way to tell that change from discovery and from redescription. | Open |
| [QUESTION-283](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-283.md) | Can composing systems create an effective structure whose adequate specification needs a richer relational vocabulary than the parts needed separately (relations of higher arity, history, or a new kind) and, if so, under what conditions, and is the new vocabulary forced by the composite or only by the restricted class of descriptions in use? | Raised at the owner's review of the pull request, which called it the result most worth preserving and asked that it "become a major research question". Hansen and Ghrist show that eliminating an interior vertex of a cellular sheaf can leave a three-way boundary relation, v₁ = v₂ + v₃, that no sheaf on the boundary's pairwise edges expresses ([THEORY-1090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1090.md); [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md)). For scalar networks reduction stays pairwise. The question asks when composition forces a change in the type of relational structure an adequate description needs. It also asks whether that is a fact about the composite or about the class of descriptions, and whether the same thing is what happens when a record's relation scheme cannot express what a composed organization requires. | Open |
| [QUESTION-287](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-287.md) | In a deterministic singularly perturbed system whose eliminated variable is fast and contracting and whose reduced system is contracting, does the memoryless quasi-steady-state reduction predict the coarse variable with an error bounded uniformly in time in terms of the eliminated dynamics? | The fast contracting case of [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md) (Active) settles it. No memory coordinate is needed: the reduction on the slow manifold stays within O(ε) of the true slow trajectory for all t ≥ 0, with every constant explicit, set by the fast contraction rate λ_z, the reduced contraction rate λ_x and the manifold's drift. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-293](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-293.md) | Is the distortion of a composite of approximate transports bounded by the sum of its parts' distortions, and does that additive bound survive when the distortion lacks a triangle inequality or a later kernel stretches distances? | The additive part of [QUESTION-017](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-017.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-260](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-260.md) (Active) settles it in full. The composite of an ε₁-transport and an ε₂-transport is an (Lε₁ + ε₂)-transport when the distortion obeys a triangle inequality, with L the later kernel's stretch, so additive when that kernel is nonexpansive, as every Markov kernel is in total variation. Without a triangle inequality, or with an expansive kernel, the additive bound fails. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-294](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-294.md) | When a network's architecture can represent a structured system's renormalization step exactly, must training by distribution fitting make the variables it represents the system's relevant ones? | The representability part of [QUESTION-060](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-060.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) (Active) settles it, in the negative. Mehta and Schwab's RBM–renormalization correspondence is an identity of parametrizations, and an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution. Away from that point a contrastive-divergence RBM spends its hidden units on noise, not on the relevant fields. The architecture's match does not fix what training keeps. | Answered |
